reason: Combine the food remainder with resident microbes to explore their interaction in the colon.
expectation: I expect the microbes to act on some of the undigested material, though I don't know what products the game will show.

effect: The microbes ferment some fibre into small fatty acids and gas, so I can now connect those contents to the body.
reaction: The distinction that microbes differ adds useful nuance.
reason: Connect the fermenting contents to the body to follow their role in the colon.
expectation: I expect the colon contents to be incorporated into the body model, possibly showing exchanges with the colon lining.

alternatives.reason: Adding mucus could establish the colon habitat first, but I want to follow the fermentation products.

effect: The model now shows fatty acids entering lining cells and blood, and water and salts moving toward capillaries.
reaction: The exchange arrows make the connection to the body clearer.
reason: Add mucus to the colon; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the mucus to appear on the colon lining, perhaps showing how it relates to the microbes.

effect: The completed model adds mucus separation, water and salt recovery, and the use of microbial fatty acids by colon cells.
reaction: The cutaway ties several exchanges together clearly, although the mucus layer’s role is shown rather than explained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding mucus brought the colon’s contents, lining and exchanges together in one planned cutaway. It showed both water recovery and where microbial fatty acids go.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the fermenting contents to the body felt somewhat transitional: it showed exchange arrows, but the final construction brought those relationships together more fully.

surprise.text: I had expected microbes to act on the remainder, but the appearance of fatty acids and gas, and the note that microbes differ, added useful detail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the final step did not explain how mucus separates most bacteria from the lining.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter: this one connected a familiar meal to microbial fermentation and the body’s use of its products. That is a personal judgment, not evidence of student comprehension or enjoyment.
